# Continual ARC task-1707cc05

## Verified transformation
In each horizontal sequence of foreground cells occurring at every other column, color the intervening cell with 2. Preserve original foreground and all other/background cells. Do not extend the sequence before its first or after its last original foreground cell. This applies independently to each row and may have other background/foreground colors.

Demo 1: background 8, foreground 1. Wherever a horizontal run had 1s with one-cell gaps (e.g. `1 8 1 8 1`), those internal gaps became 2 (`1 2 1 2 1`). Other cells unchanged. Multiple independent rows/sequences; not vertical fill.

Test (background 3, foreground 5): row 3 had 5 at columns 1 and 3 (1-based), so the gap became 2; row 5 had 5 at columns 2 and 4, likewise filled. Confirmed correct output:
```text
3 3 3 3 3 3
3 3 3 3 3 3
5 2 5 3 3 3
3 3 3 3 3 3
3 5 2 5 3 3
```

## Caution
This is not tied to the demo's colors: test foreground/background differ from demo. Detect the pattern geometrically (same-row foreground cells separated by one cell), fill only the intervening cells with color 2. Preserve all else.

## Additional verified instance (2026-10-21)
A fresh test used background 4 and foreground 8, while the demo used background 8 and foreground 6. Correct output was obtained by changing only background-4 cells lying between adjacent foreground 8s in a horizontal alternating sequence to color 2. Preserve every original 8, all other 4s, and row/column dimensions. Example: `8 4 8 4 8` becomes `8 2 8 2 8`; a pair `8 4 8` becomes `8 2 8`. This confirms the rule is color-independent: apply row-wise, only to internal one-cell gaps between matching foreground cells, with fill color fixed at 2; do not extend sequences at either end or fill vertically.
